method: five seeded PRs reviewed end to end with the real harness on the sandbox
caveat: the seeds were not all clean: adjudication was done by hand against the code, after the fact

findings.title: slugify keeps punctuation, path separators and non-ASCII characters, so its output is not a safe slug

prs.adjudication: FALSE CONFIRM: finding demands behaviour (punctuation, non-ASCII, path separators) beyond the stated docstring contract

findings.title: A negative size silently returns [] and drops every item

prs.adjudication: TRUE POSITIVE: chunk(items, -1) returns [] via range(0,n,-1); my seed was not clean

findings.title: Generators and other one-pass iterators fail with a confusing TypeError instead of being handled or clearly rejected

prs.adjudication: TRUE POSITIVE: mean(generator) raises TypeError after the emptiness check exhausts it; my seed was not clean

honest_limitation: five inputs is a smoke test. A precision figure needs tens of PRs across repos and languages with independently known defects.
